name: speckit-companion
description: 查看并掌控 AI 构建的一切。规格文档精简 60–68%，正确性不变。为 GitHub SpecKit 提供实时流水线、阶段耗时和 Living Specs，支持 Copilot、Claude、Gemini 等。

viewsWelcome.contents:
打开一个文件夹即可开始使用 SpecKit。

[$(folder-opened) 打开文件夹](command:vscode.openFolder)

已检测到 SpecKit CLI。初始化当前工作区后即可开始使用规格驱动开发。

欢迎使用 SpecKit

规格会把一个想法转化为计划和可由 AI 助手执行的任务；此面板会实时展示执行过程中的每一步。

[$(plus) 创建第一个规格](command:speckit.create)

[$(play) 打开实时示例](command:speckit.openSampleSpec)

Welcome to SpecKit

A spec turns an idea into a plan and tasks your AI assistant can implement — and this panel shows every step as it runs.

[$(plus) Create your first spec](command:speckit.create)

[$(play) Open a live sample](command:speckit.openSampleSpec)

SpecKit Companion adds living specs, lifecycle capture, and a fast-path for small changes.

[$(rocket) Install SpecKit Companion](command:speckit.companion.installNudge?%5B%22welcome%22%5D)

[Dismiss](command:speckit.companion.dismissInstallNudge)

没有规格符合当前筛选条件。

[$(globe) 创建用户规则](command:speckit.steering.createUserRule)

speckit.aiContextInstructions.description: Prepend a short context-update preamble to every SpecKit step prompt dispatched to the AI CLI, instructing the AI to keep .spec-context.json current with canonical substeps (plan.research, implement.run-tests, etc.). Disable if your AI ignores the preamble or you're debugging raw prompts.

speckit.notifications.stepComplete.description: Show a notification when a spec step or task phase completes.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code - Full feature support (steering, agents, skills, hooks)
Claude Code (VS Code) - Opens the Claude Code panel (anthropic.claude-code) and pre-fills the prompt (press Enter to send)
GitHub Copilot CLI - Steering and agents support
Codex CLI - Steering and skills support
IDE Chat - Routes prompts to the host editor's built-in AI chat (Copilot / Cursor / Windsurf)
Wibey CLI - Walmart's built-in AI coding assistant (dispatches SpecKit commands to the wibey CLI in a VS Code terminal)
Wibey (VS Code) - Opens the Wibey chat panel and pre-fills the command (uses wibey.sendPrompt when available, clipboard fallback otherwise)
Antigravity - Google's agentic coding agent (runs the `agy` CLI interactively in a VS Code terminal)
speckit.aiProvider.description: AI assistant to use for spec generation

enumDescriptions: Use provider default (Claude/Codex → dash, Gemini/Copilot/Qwen → dot)
speckit.commandFormat.description: Command format for speckit commands sent to AI CLI tools. Use 'auto' to let the provider decide, or override to 'dot' (speckit.plan) or 'dash' (speckit-plan) if your speckit version requires a specific format.

enumDescriptions: The CLI prompts before taking actions (recommended)
(YOLO) Skip all permission prompts. Faster but no review of tool calls.
speckit.permissionMode.description: Controls how the AI CLI handles permission prompts. 'interactive' is honored only by providers whose CLI supports interactive prompting (Claude, Gemini, Codex, Qwen, OpenCode). Copilot's CLI cannot surface prompts in -p mode and is auto-switched to auto-approve at dispatch time, regardless of this setting — dismissing the startup warning will not re-enable interactive mode for Copilot.

speckit.specDirectories.description: Glob patterns for spec directories. Simple names (e.g. 'specs') list their children as specs. Patterns with wildcards (e.g. 'openspec/changes/*') treat each match as a spec folder. '.specify/specs' is included by default so specs created under the SpecKit CLI's '.specify/specs/' layout are discovered. Use step-level subDir to discover sub-specs within each match.

speckit.customCommands.description: Custom SpecKit slash commands available in 'Run Custom Command'. Each entry can be a string (command name) or an object with name, title, command, step, tooltip, requiresSpecDir, and autoExecute.

command.description: Full slash command (e.g., "/speckit.review"). If omitted, name is used.

requiresSpecDir.description: Append or inject the spec directory (default: true)

autoExecute.description: Auto-run the command in the terminal (default: true)

step.description: Which phase to show this command in (spec, plan, tasks, or all)

speckit.customWorkflows.description: Custom workflow definitions for spec-driven development

displayName.description: Display name shown in workflow picker

commands.description: Custom command buttons shown next to step actions (e.g., next to Submit for specify step)

step.description: Which workflow step this command is associated with (e.g., 'specify')

steps.description: Flexible workflow steps (replaces legacy step-* keys)

command.description: Command to execute for this step, written WITHOUT a leading slash (e.g. 'speckit.specify' or 'to-spec', not '/to-spec'). A leading slash is added automatically at dispatch; if you include one it is stripped.

subFiles.description: Explicit list of sub-files shown as children in sidebar

subDir.description: Subdirectory to scan for child .md files

actionOnly.description: If true, step is action-only (no output file) and hidden from the document tree

includeRelatedDocs.description: When true, unassigned related .md files in the spec folder are grouped under this step

model.description: Claude Code model for this step, e.g. 'opus', 'sonnet', or a full model id. Passed as `claude --model <model>`. Applies only when the active AI provider is Claude Code; ignored by other providers.

effort.description: Claude Code reasoning effort for this step. Passed as `claude --effort <level>`. Applies only when the active AI provider is Claude Code; ignored by other providers.

supportedAiProviders.description: AI provider ids this workflow supports. Omit or leave empty to support all providers. When set, the workflow is hidden unless the active speckit.aiProvider is in this list (e.g. ["claude"] for a Claude-only workflow).

steering.description: Reference-doc folders/files this workflow reads but that are NOT specs (e.g. GSD's '.planning/codebase'). They appear under the Steering view and are excluded from spec detection, so they never show up as an un-created spec with a phantom phase-stepper.

label.description: Display label under the Steering view (defaults to the path's folder/file name).

enumDescriptions: SpecKit — the stock spec-driven pipeline (specify → plan → tasks → implement).
SpecKit Companion — the leaner pipeline with built-in right-sizing, through to a terminal mark-complete step. Requires the companion spec-kit extension.
speckit.defaultWorkflow.markdownDescription: Workflow pre-selected in Create Spec for new features: **SpecKit** (stock) or **SpecKit Companion** (leaner, right-sizing). Companion needs the [companion spec-kit extension](https://github.com/alfredoperez/speckit-companion#install-the-spec-kit-extension); without it, a Companion spec runs the stock commands.

speckit.companion.installPrompt.markdownDescription: Offer a one-click banner to install the companion spec-kit extension when it's missing. The banner shows whenever the extension is missing and you haven't turned this off or dismissed it.

speckit.viewer.activityPanel.markdownDescription: Show a per-spec Activity timeline in the viewer (steps, decisions, files touched). Requires the [companion spec-kit extension](https://github.com/alfredoperez/speckit-companion#install-the-spec-kit-extension).

speckit.telemetry.markdownDescription: The single on/off switch for SpecKit Companion's anonymous, PII-free usage telemetry, which helps prioritize providers and features. [What's collected](https://github.com/alfredoperez/speckit-companion#telemetry). Turning this off stops all telemetry; leaving it on still respects VS Code's global `telemetry.telemetryLevel` (if you've disabled telemetry globally, nothing is sent regardless of this switch).

walkthroughs.title: 开始使用 SpecKit Companion
walkthroughs.description: 用大约一分钟阅读一个真实规格，然后无需离开编辑器，就能把自己的想法从规格推进到计划和任务。

steps.title: 打开项目
steps.description:
SpecKit Companion reads specs out of a folder in your repo, so it needs a project open before it can show you anything.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

steps.title: 了解规格的样子
steps.description:
The quickest way to understand this extension is to read a finished spec. This copies a small sample into your specs folder and opens it in the viewer. No CLI, no AI, no setup, and clicking again reopens it rather than making a second copy.
[Open a live sample](command:speckit.openSampleSpec)

media.altText: Illustration under construction: a screenshot of the spec viewer belongs here

steps.title: 安装 Spec Kit CLI
steps.description:
Optional, and only for running phases. The viewer, review comments, and the sidebar work with no CLI at all. Install it when you want the specify, plan, tasks, and implement commands the extension dispatches to your AI.
[Install Spec Kit CLI](command:speckit.installCli)

steps.title: 配置当前项目
steps.description:
This writes the templates and phase commands your AI resolves into the repo, under a .specify folder. Reload the window once it finishes and the Specs view comes to life.
[Initialize SpecKit](command:speckit.initWorkspace)

steps.title: 编写第一个规格
steps.description:
Describe the feature in a sentence and pick the AI you already use. The extension hands it the prompt and follows along as the spec, the plan, and the tasks land on disk.
[New Spec](command:speckit.create)

steps.title: 阅读生成的概览
steps.description:
A spec with recorded activity opens on its Overview: why it exists, how long each phase took, the decisions made and what they rejected, and which test covers which requirement. It is what a reviewer reads instead of asking you again.
[How the Overview works](https://github.com/alfredoperez/speckit-companion#overview-the-runs-story)

media.altText: Illustration under construction: a screenshot of the Overview belongs here

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run compile && npm run package-web
scripts.install-local: npm version patch --no-git-tag-version && npm run package && code --install-extension speckit-companion-$(node -p "require('./package.json').version").vsix --force
